text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen defended his government's decision to link the markka to ERM in blunt exchange of words with opposition Centre Party in parliament.
- Tax authorities efforts to halt tax evasion have put hundreds of honest firms in trouble, says tax consultant.
- Professional gambling on the rise in Finland.
- Marginalised section of society chose not to vote in last weekend's municipal elections. Expert calls it a "quiet protest."
- President Martti Ahtisaari's adviser Alpo Rusi said in Berlin that Finland has left its Cold War neutrality behind.
- State-owned Postipankki will close more than 200 branch offices in more than 90 municipalities in next few years.
- Famous storybook characters, the Moomins, team up with environment ministry to promote good forest management.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Tax authorities' "commando squads" to begin cracking down on tax evasion. Tax chief says they will target companies for whom "the law is only philosophy."
- Opposition leader Esko Aho said ERM link was a bid to support the EMU project suffering from a credibility problem.
- Swedish WM-data AB, which aims to become biggest data services company in Nordic region, looking for acquisitions in Finland and Denmark, CEO said.
AAMULEHTI

- Chancellor of Justice to make inquiry into allegations that Second Finance Minister Arja Alho leaked information on Finland's ERM negotiating position to Irish finance minister and EU economic commissioner.
- On United Nations day, Finland celebrated the 40th anniversary of Finnish participation in U.N. peacekeeping activities.
DEMARI

- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said opposition leader Aho was lying when he said Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen had thought it would be best for Finland to join joint currency without ERM.
- Unemployed people from different parts of the country demonstrated in front of Parliament House demanding the right to work and human dignity.
